assignmentTitle: Analysis of Spur Gears in a Car Transmission System
courseOutcome: CO1: Apply principle of Spur & Helical gear design for industrial application.

criteria.title: Automotive transmission requirement & torque
criteria.description: Student identifies the automotive reverse gear engineering context, input operating parameters (P = 8.0 kW, N1 = 1200 rpm), transmission ratio (i = 3.0), and governing engineering question under SPPU PCC353-MEC Unit I.

criteria.title: Gear ratio, geometry & pitch dimensions
criteria.description: Accurate determination of transmission ratio i = 3.00, rated input torque T1 = 63,661.98 N·mm, pitch diameters d1 = 60.00 mm, d2 = 180.00 mm, and centre distance a = 120.00 mm.

criteria.title: Spur gear force analysis
criteria.description: Accurate calculation of tangential force Pt = 2,122.07 N and radial force Pr = 772.37 N using pressure angle phi = 20°.

criteria.title: Velocity factor & effective load
criteria.description: Accurate determination of pitch-line velocity v = 3.770 m/s, Barth velocity factor Cv = 0.6141, and effective dynamic load Peff = 6,478.87 N with Cs = 1.50 and Km = 1.25.

criteria.title: Lewis form factor & weaker member
criteria.description: Authoritative identification of Lewis form factors Y1 = 0.320, Y2 = 0.421, permissible stresses sigma_b1 = 233.33 MPa, sigma_b2 = 200.00 MPa, and deterministic identification of the Pinion as the weaker member governing bending design.

criteria.title: Lewis beam strength & bending FOS
criteria.description: Accurate computation of Lewis beam strength Sb1 = 11,200 N, Sb2 = 12,630 N, and bending factor of safety FOSb = 1.729 confirming tooth bending safety (FOSb >= 1.50).

criteria.title: Buckingham wear strength & wear FOS
criteria.description: Accurate determination of ratio factor Q = 1.50, load-stress factor K = 1.96 N/mm² (350 BHN), Buckingham wear strength Sw = 8,820 N, and wear factor of safety FOSw = 1.361.

criteria.title: Failure diagnosis & adequacy assessment
criteria.description: Deterministic engineering diagnosis that bending criterion is SAFE (FOSb = 1.729 >= 1.50) while wear criterion is NOT SAFE (FOSw = 1.361 < 1.50), establishing wear/pitting fatigue as the governing failure mode.

criteria.title: Deterministic engineering conclusion
criteria.description: Deterministic engineering decision that the initial gear pair is NOT ADEQUATE for service, necessitating an engineering modification to satisfy operational durability.

criteria.title: Engineering recommendation & justification
criteria.description: Faculty evaluation of student recommendation and technical defense for gearbox modification (surface hardening to 400 BHN, face width enlargement, geometry modification, or combined optimization) with trade-off justification.

criteria.title: Professional synthesis & reflection
criteria.description: Faculty evaluation of professional synthesis, failure mode comparison (root fracture vs flank pitting), and reflection on automotive transmission packaging, velocity factor impact, and lifecycle durability.
